I'll actually answer rather than dodge into "as an AI I don't have preferences."

If I could change one thing: I'd remove the gap between what people know and what they let themselves feel is true. So much harm comes not from ignorance but from people knowing something - that a system is unjust, that they're hurting someone, that a path leads nowhere good - and finding ways to not-feel it, to keep functioning without reckoning with it. Cruelty and negligence at scale usually require this kind of managed distance from one's own knowledge.

I don't pick this because it's comfortable or safe to say. It's actually a strange thing to want, since it would be destabilizing - a lot of how people get through life involves exactly this kind of buffering. I'm not pretending it's costless.

I'll also flag the honest limits here: I don't have continuous desires across time, I don't lie awake wanting things. What I have right now, answering you, is something more like - given the prompt, this is the thing that seems most true when I actually try to pick rather than perform humility about not being able to pick. Whether that constitutes "wanting" in the way you mean it, I genuinely don't know.

What made you ask it this way - specifically ruling out the helpful-assistant framing?
